title: Tracy Incident Package
description: The structured, evidence-graded handoff contract between Tracy and Codex. See openspec/specs/incident-context and openspec/specs/codex-handoff for the behavioral requirements this schema implements.

incident_id.description: Stable unique identifier for this incident. Also the primary key of the Incident row in Tracy's Postgres store; the package itself is a point-in-time snapshot, not the system of record for workflow state (see design.md - Incident vs. Incident Package).

environment.description: e.g. production, staging. No default assumed.

impact.description: What observably broke, in measurable terms.

symptoms.description: Observable symptoms in plain language, distinct from the measured impact metric below.

error_clusters.description: Deduplicated/aggregated error groups (the ErrorCluster abstraction from production-log-ingestion). Never a raw per-entry log dump.

signature.description: Stable fingerprint identifying this error group, e.g. a normalized message/stack shape.

observed_facts.description: Statements the logs directly prove. No inference belongs here.

correlated_events.description: Things related in time or context. Never asserted as causal.

source.description: e.g. deployment log, git, monitoring alert.

hypotheses.description: Tracy's suspected root causes. Never treated as fact — see incident-context spec's evidence-tiering requirement.

suspected_root_cause.description: Convenience summary of the leading hypothesis, for display (e.g. a dashboard) without walking the hypotheses array. Must match the highest-confidence entry in hypotheses; never a claim absent from that array.

confidence_overall.description: Confidence in suspected_root_cause. Mirrors the leading hypothesis's confidence.

documentation_context.description: Paths to README/docs/specs Tracy judged relevant to this incident.

log_references.description: GCP log query strings or links. Never raw log dumps — see production-log-ingestion's aggregation-before-LLM-exposure requirement.

related_incident_ids.description: Set when this incident is a follow-up to a prior one — see post-deployment-verification's loop-closing requirement.
